## The wall batch: one stage's wall bookings in fixed storage (`WallBatch`) {#sec-ch10-wallbatch}

<!-- PROVENANCE

### Summary

The apply of @sec-ch10-prescribed books a rate every time it runs, several times a stage, in two registers. A block
does not book those rates at each call. It copies each overwrite's differences into one device buffer and books
them all at the stage's combine. The buffer is fixed storage, not a queue, so a captured stage replays the
bookings exactly as an eager one runs them.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Book every overwrite of a stage, from both registers, at the combine, with the same launches eager and captured, @eq-ch10-flush.

**Data.** In: each overwrite's after-minus-before over the faces it wrote, flattened in the wide dtype, and its face-area weights. Out: one rate per slot booked to its register's monitor.

**Placement.** Begun in `MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance`, flushed in `MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine` before the register's `end_stage`.

**Activation.** Always on a MeshBlock; a register without a batch books at the call.

**Guarantee / limits.** Each slot's rows are a plain weighted sum: deterministic, no scatter-add.

**Evidence.** `test_flux_register.<b>`; `test_graph_monitor_amounts.<b>` on CUDA (Tests).
:::

Local symbols: $k$[^rg-362f2334766b] is a slot of the batch, $\delta_k$ its flattened after-minus-before, $w_k$ its face-area
weights laid out the same way, $\mathcal R_k$ the set of entries of row $r$ in slot $k$.

### Derivation

None beyond @eq-ch10-overwrite: the batch defers the sum, it does not change it. At the flush, slot $k$ books for
each of its rows

$$
a_{k,r} = \sum_{i\in\mathcal R_k} \delta_{k,i}\,w_{k,i},
$$ {#eq-ch10-flush}

which is @eq-ch10-overwrite for the faces that overwrite wrote, computed later.

### Numerical method

**One batch per block.** `MeshBlockImpl::reset` makes one `WallBatch` and gives it to the hydro register and the
scalar register ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}). `overwrite_` pushes to it when it is
set ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::overwrite_ >}}).

**Slots in push order.** A push takes the next slot of the stage
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::slot_ >}}). A slot is identified by the monitor it books to, the
amount index, the number of rows, the number of entries and the weights tensor itself. If the slot at the cursor
matches, it is reused; otherwise the slots from the cursor on are rebuilt and the buffer is laid out again, keeping
the slots before it ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::layout_ >}}). So a register and direction
applied twice in a stage, before and after the implicit correction, takes two slots, and a register whose weights
were rebuilt gets a new slot rather than its first weights. `push` copies the differences into the slot's place in the
buffer ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::push >}}).

**The flush.** `flush` books every slot with @eq-ch10-flush, one product with the weights and one sum over each
slot's entries per row, through `book_index`, then zeroes the buffer
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::flush >}}). The comment on the weights says why it is a plain sum:
a scatter-add on CUDA is not deterministic, and the captured path must equal the eager path bitwise
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.hpp WallBatch >}}).

**In the stage.** `stage_advance` resets the cursor at the start of every stage and clears the buffer at stage 0,
which drops a rejected attempt's bookings ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}}).
`stage_combine` flushes before the register's `end_stage`, so the stage's wall rates land in that stage's slot of the
amounts ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine >}}).

**Why fixed storage.** The header records the failure a host queue had: a user forcing splits the stage into a
captured advance and a captured combine, the combine's first warm-up drained the queue, its capture recorded no
flush, and its replays never ran the host push again. The state stayed equal and the wall rates were lost under
graph ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.hpp WallBatch >}}). The buffer is therefore registered with the state store
as `wall_batch`, with the monitor's count buffers, so the executor's save list restores it around a warm-up
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::register_flux_storage >}}).

| `test_graph_monitor_amounts.<b>` (`user_forcing_graph_books_wall_rates_like_eager`) | with a user forcing between a captured advance and a captured combine, every amount on the graph block equals the eager block's, across a replay and a redo | exact (`torch::equal`) | graph must equal eager ({{< code tests/test_graph_monitor_amounts.cpp GraphSaveList.user_forcing_graph_books_wall_rates_like_eager >}}); CUDA only |

The first passes at the pin, on CPU. The second skips without CUDA and was not run here (@tbl-ch10-ctest-run).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A slot is registered at its first push, eagerly; the header states that this happens before any capture
  ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.hpp WallBatch >}}). A push pattern that first appears inside a capture is
  outside that statement, and this chapter found no test of it.
:::

1. **Graph evidence is CUDA only.** The one test that compares the batch under capture with eager needs CUDA; on
   this report's CPU run it is skipped.
